channel.title: RISC-V Distros — All updates
channel.description: Which RISC-V distribution runs on which board, where to get images, and the pitfalls to expect.

item.title: Boards — SpacemiT K3 (Pico-ITX / CoM260)
item.description: 8× X100 @2.4GHz + 8× A100 AI cores, RVA23/RVV1.0 (up to 1024-bit), 60 TOPS general AI compute, 130 KDMIPS. Pico-ITX: 16/32GB LPDDR5-6400, UFS2.2 128/256GB, 10GbE SFP+ + 1GbE, 2× M.2 (M-Key Gen3 x4 / B-Key), 2× USB3.2 Type-C (full-featured 65W PD + 4K DP) + 4× USB2.0, 100×86mm. CoM260: a 260-pin compute module plus a reference carrier board, the carrier being hardware-compatible with Jetson Orin Nano.

item.title: Distros — openEuler
item.description: An RISC-V base for server/enterprise use, moving fastest on RVA23 + Server Platform; unless you are validating server scenarios, RevyOS/Bianbu will save you trouble on a dev board. ｜ Based on openEuler 24.03 LTS (RPM/dnf, own repos) + RVCK 6.6 kernel; RISC-V ships as two separate builds, RVA20 and RVA23

item.title: Distros — RHEL RISC-V Developer Preview
item.description: An enterprise-oriented RISC-V preview: use it to check whether the RHEL userland runs, but for day-to-day use Debian / Ubuntu / RevyOS are less trouble. ｜ Based on RHEL 10.2 (Fedora / CentOS Stream 10 code base)

item.title: Distros — AlmaLinux OS Kitten 10
item.description: The first downstream distribution in the RHEL family to publish official riscv64 builds; without a board at hand, the GenericCloud image under QEMU lets you try it right away. ｜ Based on CentOS Stream 10 (RHEL 10 code base)

item.title: Distros — Rocky Linux 10
item.description: If you want the RHEL 10 userland on RISC-V without touching a Red Hat account, the riscv64 container images of Rocky 10 are the ready-to-use option today; running a real system still means waiting for installation media. ｜ Based on RHEL 10 (CentOS Stream 10 code base)

item.title: Distros — Debian
item.description: Debian is the only independent distro here that made riscv64 an official release architecture; separately there are Debian-based riscv64 systems such as deepin and RevyOS (not verified one by one). ｜ Based on Independent

item.title: Distros — Ubuntu
item.description: Ubuntu has the most detailed board support: it publishes preinstalled images per board, but 26.04 raised the bar to RVA23, leaving older boards stuck on 24.04 LTS. ｜ Based on Debian

item.title: Distros — Fedora
item.description: Fedora runs an official RISC-V SIG with continuous builds, but the project still labels riscv64 "not officially supported" and ships images through the alt channel. It works fine day to day; its support level is simply not the same as Debian or Ubuntu. ｜ Based on Independent

item.title: Distros — Fedora-V Force (FVF)
item.description: FVF is a RISC-V image rebuilt from Fedora sources by a separate team, not an official Fedora release. It covers more boards than the official SIG images, so it is the practical pick when you want a Fedora userland that boots out of the box. ｜ Based on Fedora

item.title: Distros — RevyOS
item.description: The de facto standard on TH1520 boards: LicheePi 4A and Milk-V Meles ship with RevyOS, and the official tutorials flash it too. The best first pick for newcomers, but note that the mirror is newer than the docs — take the latest date from the mirror directory. ｜ Based on Debian 13 (trixie) rootfs + XuanTie-customized 6.6 kernel (TH1520/SG2042 BSP); the older 20240720 build is Debian 12 + 5.10 kernel

item.title: Distros — Bianbu
item.description: The only system with an official desktop experience on K1/K3 boards (BPI-F3, Milk-V Jupiter, MUSE, Pico-ITX): GNOME/LXQt out of the box and complete documentation, making it the friendliest vendor distro for newcomers. ｜ Based on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (Bianbu 2.x, K1) / Ubuntu 25.04 (Bianbu 3.x, K1) / Ubuntu 26.04 (Bianbu 4.x, K3; per vendor forum, not stated per release in official docs) + vendor BSP kernel 6.6 LTS / 6.18

item.title: Distros — openKylin
item.description: The RISC-V branch of a domestic desktop OS, with board coverage split across versions (3.0 only knows K3/V100). Good for evaluating a domestic desktop stack, not as a daily driver on older TH1520/K1 boards. ｜ Based on Independent build (deb/APT + own repos, UKUI desktop); 3.0 uses a Linux 7.0 kernel, 2.0 SP2 is the long-term stable release

item.title: Distros — deepin
item.description: The best-looking domestic desktop distro, but its RISC-V branch is a community preview shipped as per-board tar.xz files — fine for evaluation, not recommended as your only daily system. ｜ Based on Debian-based + deepin's own repos (deepin 25 "crimson"); kernel 6.6/6.12/6.16 depending on board, mainline kernel on DP1000

item.title: Distros — Armbian
item.description: The main reason domestic RISC-V boards are usable out of the box; look here first for newer boards like K3/BPI-F3. ｜ Based on Debian/Ubuntu (Armbian build framework)

item.title: Distros — Alpine Linux
item.description: Alpine's riscv64 is a real architecture, but board coverage is narrow — there are only those five u-boot packages, so anything outside them means porting it yourself. ｜ Based on Independent

item.title: Distros — Arch Linux RISC-V
item.description: Arch's "official" here is only the port's own tested list, not official Arch support — the page should mark it as a community port. ｜ Based on Arch Linux

item.title: Distros — openSUSE
item.description: MicroOS is a riscv64 variant of the same project (there is a kvm-and-xen qcow2 image), not a downstream derivative. ｜ Based on Independent

item.title: Distros — Gentoo
item.description: Friendly to veterans, discouraging for beginners: complete docs but a fully manual install, good for people who want deep customization or an embedded rootfs. ｜ Based on Independent (built from source, OpenRC/systemd optional)

item.title: Distros — NixOS
item.description: Declarative config is nice, but riscv64 is in a "it runs, don't expect an easy ride" state. ｜ Based on Independent (Nix/nixpkgs, systemd)

item.title: Distros — FreeBSD
item.description: If you want a proper Unix-like system with official images, FreeBSD is the most solid non-Linux option on RISC-V. ｜ Based on Independent (BSD, FreeBSD kernel + pkg)

item.title: Distros — NetBSD
item.description: Smooth under QEMU; on real hardware it depends on whether you already have a working U-Boot. ｜ Based on Independent (BSD, NetBSD kernel + pkgsrc)

item.title: Distros — OpenBSD
item.description: Security-focused and minimal; the experience is most orthodox on an Unmatched, otherwise not a beginner's pick. ｜ Based on Independent (BSD, OpenBSD kernel + ports/packages)

item.title: Distros — ALT Linux
item.description: The most complete RISC-V support among Russian distros, with images that work out of the box; suited to QEMU and Unmatched users. ｜ Based on Independent (RPM/apt-rpm, ALT's own toolchain)

item.title: Distros — Buildroot
item.description: Make it clear to newcomers: this is not a distro but a toolbox for building your own. ｜ Based on Built from source (BusyBox/glibc/musl + optional packages)

item.title: Distros — Yocto / OpenEmbedded
item.description: Aimed at industrial/production use; hobbyists should start with Armbian or Buildroot instead. ｜ Based on Built from source (BitBake + oe-core + meta-riscv)

item.title: Distros — openRuyi
item.description: Mostly for vendor/ecosystem testing: it is officially positioned as early validation — surfacing firmware, platform-semantics and kernel interop problems early so vendors fork less. Regular users normally don't need it; for daily use pick a vendor distro such as Bianbu / RevyOS / openKylin, and try its QEMU image if you just want a zero-cost look. ｜ Based on Independent, self-built (RPM + dnf, rolling release); kernel 7.2.6 / LTS 6.18.54, toolchain GCC 16.2 with its own glibc

item.title: Distros — Void Linux
item.description: Not usable for any RISC-V scenario right now; listed only to show that "small and fast" does not mean "has RISC-V". ｜ Based on Independent (XBPS + runit + musl/glibc)

item.title: Distros — PLD Linux
item.description: Treat it as "no RISC-V support"; mark it as unsupported on the portal rather than misleading readers. ｜ Based on Independent (RPM + poldek, Polish community distro)

item.title: Distros — Slackware
item.description: Long-time Slackware users can try slarm64 to keep the habit alive on RISC-V; beginners should stay away. ｜ Based on Independent (pkgtools + slackpkg, BSD-style init)

item.title: Distros — Android (AOSP)
item.description: Only for experiments that check whether the Android framework boots on RISC-V — don't treat it as a usable system. ｜ Based on AOSP (Linux kernel + Android framework)

item.title: Boards — QEMU virt (virtual machine)
item.description: Pure virtual platform: up to 512 RV64GC cores, CLINT/PLIC, a PCIe host bridge, 8 virtio-mmio devices, NS16550 UART, optional AIA/IOMMU; memory, disks and networking are all virtualised through command-line options, with no real GPU/VPU/NPU.
item.category: None (generic QEMU virtual platform, RV32/RV64 configurable, up to 512 cores)

item.title: Boards — StarFive VisionFive 2
item.description: 2/4/8GB LPDDR4, microSD + eMMC (some versions), M.2 M-Key NVMe, 2× GbE (v1.3 supports PoE), HDMI 2.0, 4× USB, 40-pin GPIO; there is also a cut-down VisionFive 2 Lite.
item.category: StarFive JH7110: 4×SiFive U74 @1.5GHz + S7 monitor core + E24

item.title: Boards — LicheePi 4A
item.description: 4/8/16GB LPDDR4X, 8/32/128GB eMMC, 2× GbE, WiFi5/BT5, HDMI 2.0 + 4-lane MIPI DSI, 2× MIPI CSI, 4× USB3, 40-pin GPIO.

item.title: Boards — Milk-V Meles
item.description: 4/8/16GB LPDDR4X 4266MT/s, eMMC socket (optional module) + microSD, 1× GbE (PoE capable), WiFi5/BT5.2 (AP6256), 4× USB3.0, HDMI 2.0 4K60, MIPI DSI/CSI, 40-pin, credit-card sized.

item.title: Boards — Zhihe A210 (XuanTie MelonPi dev board)
item.description: 8-core 64-bit RISC-V: 4× C920 @1.9GHz + 4× C908 @1.9GHz, all with RVV (128-bit); NPU 12 TOPS@INT8 supporting INT4/INT8/FP8/FP16/BF16 and Transformers; LPDDR4X up to 16GB; eMMC5.1; H.265 decode 4K@120fps; the board is a SODIMM compute module plus V1/V2/V3 open carrier boards, 8GB LPDDR4X + 32GB eMMC (figures from a third-party project page)

item.title: Boards — Canaan K230 (Kendryte K230 / CanMV-K230)
item.description: Dual-core 64-bit RISC-V C908: big core 1.6GHz with RVV1.0, little core 0.8GHz; KPU rated at 6 TOPS equivalent (INT8/INT16) (1 TOPS on the K230D); the CanMV-K230 board carries 512MB LPDDR4, microSD, HDMI, 3× MIPI-CSI and USB; typical chip power is about 2W

item.title: Boards — Milk-V Megrez (ESWIN EIC7700X)
item.description: 4× SiFive P550 @1.8GHz (RV64GBCH, ships at 1.4GHz/800mV); 19.95 TOPS@INT8 NPU; IMG AXM-8-256 GPU (OpenGL ES3.2/Vulkan1.2/OpenCL); 8/16/32GB LPDDR5-6400; Mini-ITX 170×170mm; PCIe x8 slot (Gen3 x4), 2× GbE, 4× USB3, SATA/M.2 SATA, 8K H.265 encode/decode

item.title: Boards — Milk-V Titan (UltraRISC DP1000)
item.description: 8× UR-CP100 @2.0GHz, RV64GCBHX (full RVA22, no V extension); up to 64GB DDR4 UDIMM (ECC supported); PCIe Gen4 x16, NVMe Gen4 x4, 2× GbE, USB3; Mini-ITX; UEFI+ACPI+SMBIOS; optional BMC module; no onboard display output

item.title: Boards — SiFive HiFive Unmatched
item.description: 16GB DDR4 onboard, PCIe x16 (for a GPU/NVMe), M.2 Key M, M.2 Key E (WiFi), GbE, 4× USB 3.0, microSD, SPI Flash; microATX form factor with 12V barrel power.

item.title: Boards — Banana Pi BPI-F3 (SpacemiT K1)
item.description: 8× X60 (RV64GCVB, RVA22, RVV1.0), 2.0 TOPS; IMG BXE-2-32 GPU @819MHz; 2/4/8/16GB LPDDR4; 8/16/32/128GB eMMC; 2× GbE, 4× USB3.0, HDMI1.4 (1080p), PCIe2.1 (M.2 M-Key + mini PCIe), WiFi6/BT5.2; 148×100mm

item.title: Boards — Orange Pi RV2 (Ky X1)
item.description: 8-core 64-bit RISC-V (single-core performance about 1.3× a Cortex-A55), 2 TOPS fused CPU compute (no dedicated NPU); 2/4/8GB LPDDR4X; optional 16–128GB eMMC module; 2× M.2 M-Key (PCIe2.0 x2, NVMe capable), 2× GbE, WiFi5/BT5, 3× USB3 + 2× USB2, HDMI, 89×56mm

item.title: Boards — SiFive HiFive Premier P550
item.description: 4× SiFive P550 @1.4GHz (out-of-order); 16/32GB LPDDR5-6400 + 128GB eMMC; 20 TOPS NPU; Imagination GPU; Mini-DTX; PCIe Gen3 x4 (x16 slot), 2× GbE, 5× USB3, SATA; Ubuntu 24.04 preinstalled (6.6 kernel, OTA supported)

item.title: Boards — StarFive VisionFive 2 Lite (JH7110S)
item.description: 4× RV64GC @1.25GHz + IMG BXE-4-32 MC1 GPU; 2/4/8GB LPDDR4; WiFi6/BT5.4; M.2 (PCIe2.0 x1), GbE, USB2.0/3.0, HDMI 4K@60, 40-pin GPIO, MIPI-CSI/DSI; microSD/eMMC

item.title: Boards — BeagleV-Ahead
item.description: 4GB LPDDR4, 16GB onboard eMMC, WiFi5/BT5 (AP6203BM), GbE, microHDMI, microSD, 2× CSI + 1× DSI, mikroBUS, BeagleBone Black cape headers.

item.title: Boards — Milk-V Pioneer (SG2042, server-oriented)
item.description: 4× DDR4 DIMM up to 128GB (ECC RDIMM/UDIMM), 3× PCIe x16 (Gen3 x8 signalling), 5× SATA, 2× 2.5GbE, 8× USB3, 2× M.2, an eMMC module connector, microSD; mATX 24.4×24.4cm with standard 24-pin ATX power, 120W typical.

item.title: Boards — Milk-V Duo series (Duo / Duo 256M / Duo S)
item.description: Duo: 2× C906 (1GHz + 700MHz) + an 8051, 64MB SIP DRAM; Duo 256M: SG2002 plus 1× Cortex-A53, 256MB; Duo S: 512MB + eMMC pads (some kits ship 8GB) + WiFi6; all have a 100M Ethernet port and USB-C; Duo/256M are 26-pin GPIO pads at 21×51mm, Duo S has 2× 26-pin headers at 43×43mm.
